title: The Origins of Fantasy Fiction
use_cases: Use when researching the historical evolution of supernatural literature
Implement when categorizing sub-genres within modern fiction
Configure when defining the core characteristics of high and urban fantasy
Use when teaching the distinction between ancient myths and modern genre fiction
content:
Fantasy fiction is very old. Its roots go back to ancient myths, legends, and fairy tales from all over the world. Think of the Greek myths. Think of King Arthur. These are stories of heroes, gods, and magic. This is the deep root of myth vs reality in literature.

Modern fantasy, as we know it, really started in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Writers like J.R.R. Tolkien and C.S. Lewis are often called the “fathers” of modern fantasy. They were scholars who loved old myths. They wanted to create their own. Their fantasy storytelling techniques mixed epic quests with deep, detailed worlds.

Today, fantasy is a huge genre. It has many sub-genres. There is high fantasy (like Tolkien). There is urban fantasy (like The Dresden Files). There is dark fantasy. But they all share that core idea of a supernatural world or element.
